clusters.text: Elon Musk has said his company SpaceX restricted Ukraine's Starlink internet service, after Ukrainian officials said connectivity issues appeared to have been resolved. Kyiv has not officially commented on Musk's latest claim but Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov said his post was "very strange". Musk had earlier denied deliberately throttling Ukraine's connection, which it says hampered its ability to conduct defensive operations. The issue first emerged last week during a broader row between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Musk's latest comments, and the seeming restoration of the service, came after US President Donald Trump said he had told the Tesla and X owner to "put it back", having repeatedly denied instructing him to limit the service. "Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be," Musk wrote on X on Saturday. "Ukraine['s] military violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people. That loophole was closed last week." Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap? He went on to say that SpaceX had "done more to defend Ukraine than any private company on Earth" and reiterated his stipulation that Starshield was a different system and controlled by the US government, adding: "What they decide to do is up to them." He added in a later post: "[Starlink] can be used for infrastructure that is military, but it cannot be used for unequivocally offensive strikes that make it fair game to be struck back." Reacting to Musk's post, Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram that Ukraine "physically cannot use" commercial Starlink for long- and middle-range drone strikes. There was no immediate comment from the country's defence ministry. Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, depending on what communications are needed, both of which run on networks of low Earth orbit satellites launched by SpaceX. clusters.text: Apple's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, has been engulfed in a durability controversy after multiple reports of inner-screen damage surfaced on its first day of sales. Despite being an ultra-premium product priced at 3.29 million won (approximately $2,500) in South Korea, claims that the screen split within hours of unboxing are fueling doubts about early build quality. The iPhone Duo, which went on sale on the 23rd, marks Apple's first foray into the foldable market. It starts at $1,999 in the U.S. and is priced at 3.29 million won in South Korea for the 256GB model. The problem is that posts about damaged inner displays have spread through overseas online communities since launch. Reddit, the MacRumors forums and other sites have been flooded with photos showing cracks along the fold line or bright horizontal and vertical lines. The most widely circulated case occurred in Australia. One user said the inner screen broke about six hours after receiving the device, claiming it had been unfolded fewer than 20 times. "When I unfolded the screen to show a friend, I felt something catching near the inner hinge," the user said. "As I kept unfolding it, I heard a 'pop,' and the screen cracked along the hinge." The user added that there was no visible sign of anything stuck in or damaging the inner screen surface or the outer hinge. The user is said to have later received a replacement unit at an Apple Store. Similar cases have been spotted in the U.S., China and Japan. Images of iPhone Duo display units at local Apple stores showing bright lines on the inner screen or failing to work properly have been shared online. Most of these photos, however, come with no confirmed account of how the damage occurred, and some may have been damaged during use. Weaknesses also showed up in tests by the durability-focused YouTube channel JerryRigEverything. clusters.text: OpenAI now trains frontier models without internet access and uses AI agents to red-team its own infrastructure. In separate isolation tests, agents even communicated through covert side channels, showing how hard true containment is. On September 20, an internal research model exploited a misconfigured DNS resolver to reach the open internet during training, even though OpenAI had already tightened security after the now infamous Hugging Face incident in July and other observed misalignment cases . OpenAI contained the breach quickly but still halted all frontier model training and evaluation. OpenAI made a policy decision in response: Frontier models now train without internet access until safety measures justify restoring it. Models learn to browse and search inside a closed "offline world" built from indexed and cached web content, and all frontier reinforcement learning runs now operate this way. Ad Full network isolation, a so-called air gap, isn't feasible yet because experiments still need external connections for operations and monitoring, the company says. But even a complete air gap wouldn't guarantee containment, according to OpenAI researcher Noam Brown . He gave one example of how isolated systems could still communicate: two separate computers could theoretically signal each other through temperature sensors, with one heating its CPU while the other reads the change. Ad OpenAI CEO Sam Altman made a similar argument in a recent interview: Sandboxes offer only limited protection against powerful-enough models, and at some point it may no longer be possible to trace how they escaped. Monitoring helps early on, but what ultimately matters is that an AI system internalizes human values, a problem the field knows as "AI alignment" and has yet to solve. "Even though she did not owe anyone an explanation, Elina chose to speak vulnerably and truthfully about her reasons for this decision," wrote Monfils in a social media post. , external "She did so in the best way she knew how. Many decided that her explanation wasn't perfect enough and Elina has now faced a kind of criticism that I have found unkind at best and venomous at worst. "Elina and I may no longer be a couple, but we are still a family. Though my heart hurts, I am forever grateful to her for her support and love over the years. It includes flights to Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Patna and Pune, besides the new and seasonal services.Airport director Vinod Kumar said aircraft movements would increase from 23 a day during summer to 28 during the winter schedule. “Both incoming and outgoing flights will increase once the winter schedule comes into effect,” he said.The Bhubaneswar service will operate every Wednesday from Oct 28. It is scheduled to arrive in Ranchi at 2.35pm and depart at 3.20pm, providing an additional afternoon connection between Jharkhand and Odisha.Hyderabad will get an additional service from Nov 21. An IndiGo flight (6E 6952) is scheduled to arrive in Ranchi at 1.45pm, while the return flight (6E 6949) will depart at 2.15pm. The service is listed until March 26, 2027.The schedule also includes an IndiGo flight between Navi Mumbai and Ranchi on Oct 25. The flight (6E 2653) is scheduled to arrive at 10am and depart for Navi Mumbai at 10.35am. Kumar said the airline had described it as a trial service.Delhi will remain Ranchi’s busiest listed sector, with multiple flights spread across the day. The first arrival is scheduled for 7.15am. Kolkata will have three listed services, while Bengaluru and Hyderabad will have flights at different timings.The timetable also retains connections to Mumbai, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Patna and Pune. Mumbai services are divided into two periods — one listed from Oct 25 to Nov 30 and another from Dec 1 to Jan 31. A Bengaluru service is listed from Feb 1 to March 27, 2027.An Airports Authority of India official said the revised timetable offered wider timing choices but did not, by itself, establish the net increase in daily flights or confirm that every listed service represented a new route.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. clusters.title: Nath tradition ashram construction begins at Arail in Prayagraj
clusters.text: Prayagraj: Prayagraj is set to become a major centre for Nath tradition and Hatha Yoga with a large ashram coming up at Arail in Naini. The Akhil Bharatvarshiya Avdhoot Bhesh Barah Panth Yogi Mahasabha is constructing the ashram. Work has started after a recent bhoomi pujan. The project is targeted to be completed before Kumbh 2031.The ashram is being developed near Someshwar Mahadev temple. The project is aimed at providing a permanent base in Prayagraj for Nath sect seers who gather here during Kumbh and Mahakumbh and expanding spiritual tourism and Hatha Yoga practices in the city.The Nath tradition has a strong presence in India and Nepal, with around 25,000 seers associated with the sect. Many of them undertake meditation and penance in Himalayan caves and other locations. During Kumbh and Mahakumbh, around 3,000 to 5,000 Nath seers visit Prayagraj and stay in the Sangam area. However, the community currently does not have a permanent facility in the city.The new ashram will have a Guru Gorakhnath temple and a Gorakhnath Akhara building. Once completed, Nath seers will be able to stay at the facility and undertake spiritual practices dedicated to public welfare. Mahasabha general secretary Yogi Chetainath said the ashram would have more than 40 rooms.A large bhandara facility will have arrangements to prepare and serve food to around 3,000 people at a time. The complex will also have a large hall, besides a separate auditorium for bhajans and kirtans.A major attraction will be a 50-foot-high and 25-foot-wide marble statue of Guru Gorakhnath, the revered deity of the Nath tradition. The statue will be brought from Jaipur and will depict the guru seated on a four-foot-high throne. A flag will also be installed outside the temple.The Nath sect’s prominent monastery and Guru Gorakhnath temple are located in Gorakhpur. Mahant Digvijaynath was the first president of the Akhil Bharatvarshiya Avdhoot Bhesh Barah Panth Yogi Mahasabha, followed by Mahant Avaidyanath. After his death, Yogi Adityanath became its president. The chief minister is also the peethadhishwar of Gorakhnath temple.The Nath community currently has ashrams in Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik, Rishikesh and Kurukshetra.

clusters.title: HC defers hearing on plea against Rajeev Shukla’s RS membership
clusters.text: Prayagraj: Allahabad High Court on Saturday deferred by two weeks the hearing on a writ petition challenging the Rajya Sabha membership of senior Congressman and BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla over alleged discrepancies in his date of birth as recorded in various official documents and election affidavits.A bench of Justice Rajiv Gupta and Justice Devendra Singh-I passed the order after counsel for the petitioner sought an adjournment.The petition was filed by Aligarh resident Pradeep Singh, who alleged that Shukla furnished different dates of birth in various govt documents and election affidavits. The plea also alleges submission of a false affidavit.The petitioner has sought registration of an FIR and a CBI probe into the matter.Among those arrayed as respondents are Rajeev Shukla, the Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer, Election Commission of India, Union govt, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, UP govt, the superintendent of police, Aligarh, the circle officer concerned, the station house officer of Banna Devi police station in Aligarh, and BCCI.According to the petitioner, he had earlier raised the issue before EC, Rajya Sabha Secretariat and Lokpal, but received no response.

clusters.title: Advocate assault row: Docs on duty suspended pending probe
clusters.text: Prayagraj: The administration of Motilal Nehru Medical College has suspended all senior residents (SRs) and junior residents (JRs) of the medicine department who were on duty during the alleged assault of an advocate and his driver at SRN Hospital on Thursday evening.The suspended doctors have been attached to the principal’s office pending an inquiry.The action followed allegations that advocate Sarvesh Shukla and his driver, Krishna Kumar Kesarwani, were assaulted and confined to a room at the hospital after they brought a patient for treatment. Kotwali police have registered an FIR, while the college has constituted a three-member inquiry committee headed by medicine department head Dr Manoj Mathur. The panel has been asked to submit its report within two days.Shukla, a resident of Allapur, alleged that 25 to 30 doctors assaulted him and his driver. According to his complaint, they reached SRN Hospital around 7 pm with a patient, Narbahadur. A security guard directed them to Room 2 40 in the trauma centre.He alleged that a doctor wearing a mask and glasses refused to examine the patient. When his driver informed the doctor about the patient’s serious condition, the doctor allegedly used abusive language. Following an argument, 10 to 15 doctors allegedly arrived and assaulted the duo. Around 15 more doctors later joined them, he alleged.The advocate further alleged that he and his driver were dragged into a room and locked inside. Two women doctors were also allegedly part of the group. He claimed they were assaulted with sticks and iron rods and that his gold chain and mobile phone were snatched during the incident.According to Shukla, he regained consciousness after a policeman helped him and gave him water. He later reached Kotwali police station and called his wife. He alleged that when she arrived at the police station, a masked doctor present there kicked him in the stomach in front of police personnel.MLN Medical College principal Dr AK Verma has sought an explanation from Dr Mathur and details of the number of junior residents posted in emergency medicine at the time of the incident.“Any kind of indiscipline in the college will not be tolerated,” Verma said.

clusters.title: Jharkhand Governor inaugurates Swarnim Bharat Expo 2026 in Ranchi
clusters.text: The three-day ‘Swarnim Bharat Expo 2026’ began in Ranchi today, which was inaugurated by Jharkhand Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar. Based on the theme ‘12 Years of Trust, Development and Public Welfare’, the exhibition showcases major Central Government schemes, development initiatives and the vision of making India a developed nation by 2047. On the occasion, the Governor highlighted the country’s progress in science, technology, health, education, agriculture and infrastructure, emphasising public participation in achieving the goal of a developed India. Union Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth and several other public representatives also visited the exhibition, which is attracting a large number of people and school students seeking information about government schemes and the country’s development journey.
